items.title: Meta opened Muse and exposed its risks
items.oneliner: Meta opened Muse connectors, then researchers pulled 6.8 GB including SSH keys. Agent platforms are already a security boundary.

items.title: Go is finally getting portable SIMD
items.oneliner: Go 1.26 and 1.27 add experimental SIMD APIs, making near-assembly vector code realistic without handwritten assembly.

items.title: Google wants ML infrastructure in orbit
items.oneliner: Google plans TPU tests in low Earth orbit, betting constant solar power could become the next AI infrastructure moat.

items.title: File notifications became a cross-platform side channel
items.oneliner: Researchers say file-notification APIs on Linux, Android, Windows, and macOS can reconstruct user behavior with minimal permissions.

items.title: SourceHut had an account takeover bug
items.oneliner: A SourceHut XSS in ansi2html let attackers hijack accounts through build logs, turning CI output into an attack surface.

items.title: Radicle disclosed protocol-level privacy failures
items.oneliner: Radicle says all released versions leak unauthenticated, unencrypted node traffic, so private repositories should stop using the network.

items.title: Power is now the AI bottleneck
items.oneliner: Oracle may owe data center investors even without electricity. AI infrastructure is now constrained by megawatts, not model ambition.

items.title: Omnibin challenges package installation itself
items.oneliner: Omnibin mounts every nixpkgs binary on demand, pushing package management toward lazy access instead of preinstalled toolchains.

items.title: The Dutch government is backing NixOS
items.oneliner: The Netherlands is building a NixOS-based workplace alternative to Microsoft, turning reproducibility into a public-sector sovereignty strategy.

items.title: CUDA optimization is becoming agent work
items.oneliner: An agentic CUDA optimizer now generates, benchmarks, and iterates kernels automatically, hinting at a new workflow for GPU performance engineering.
